title: How costumes in the new 'Sense and Sensibility' show two sisters sharing clothes
summary:
A new movie version of "Sense and Sensibility," based on Jane Austen's first novel, is now in theaters. It follows two sisters: sensible Elinor, played by Daisy Edgar-Jones, and romantic Marianne, played by Esmé Creed-Miles. Costume designer Grace Snell told IndieWire how she used clothes to tell their story.

The story takes place in the Regency era in England, more than 200 years ago. Snell had never designed costumes for a historical film before. She did deep research on the period, but she also wanted the clothes to feel modern. She was inspired by fashion from the 1990s and early 2000s, which had a similar shape to dresses from Austen's time.

Her biggest idea came from real life: sisters often borrow each other's clothes. After the Dashwood family has to leave its home and move to a small cottage in Devonshire, the sisters share, adapt and mix their outfits.

Snell said she could tell the two actors' characters apart right away at their first fittings. Elinor's fitting was organized and labeled. For Marianne, Snell brought boxes of ribbons, trims and hats and let the actor dress herself, even if things were not done up correctly. Marianne ends up with a playful, slightly rebellious style, including old dresses that are a bit too big.

Snell also gave both sisters jackets cut from the same pattern, in the same color but different fabrics. Elinor's jacket was made longer. "They could wear the same outfit, but they were styled differently," Snell said.

The cheerful Mrs. Jennings, played by Fiona Shaw, got bold outfits too. "I had a lot of fun with Fiona," Snell said.
why_it_matters: The story shows how clothes in movies are carefully planned to show characters' personalities and relationships, not just the time period.
